title.drive: Main menu entry: go out on track alone (practice). Short, it sits in a narrow menu rail.
title.driveQuickSetup: Small line under Drive on the very first visit: Drive opens a short setup first.
title.driveTimedRun: Small line under Drive on a hill climb: one timed run from start to finish.
title.raceAi: Main menu entry: a race against computer-controlled cars. AI = artificial intelligence; keep it as AI if your language uses that abbreviation.
title.raceAiDetail: Line under Race AI. {opponents}: number of AI cars. {skill}: the AI's skill level, already translated. {start}: empty, or ' · ' plus the start type (e.g. ' · Rolling start').
title.multiplayerEntered: Badge beside Multiplayer: you have joined the next open race.
title.multiplayerInLobby: Badge beside Multiplayer: how many players are in your room's lobby (always 2 or more).
title.challenge: Main menu entry: the weekly time-trial challenge.
title.challengeShort: Shorter form of 'Weekly challenge' for narrow phone tabs.
title.challengeDetail: {timeLeft}: e.g. '3 d 4 h', already formatted. {circuit}: circuit name, not translated.
title.carLocked: The car can't be changed during an online race. {car}: car name, not translated.
title.conditions: Main menu entry: weather and time of day.
title.garage: Main menu entry: car setup (tyres, wings, suspension).
title.garageTyres: {compound}: tyre compound name such as Soft or Wet, already translated.
title.lapTimes: Main menu entry: lap time boards.
title.feedback: Main menu entry: send a bug report, a request or an idea.
title.press: Main menu link to the press page.
title.support: Link to the developer's tip page (Buy Me a Coffee). Translate the meaning ('support the developer') if the phrase doesn't work in your language.
prompts.move: Button prompt at the bottom of the screen: the stick or arrow keys move the cursor.
prompts.select: Button prompt: confirm the highlighted item.
prompts.closePanel: Button prompt. {panel}: the open panel's title, already translated.
prompts.switchPanel: Button prompt: shoulder buttons switch between panels.
prompts.page: Button prompt: triggers turn the board's pages.
upNext.region: Screen-reader name of the card showing the circuit and car you'll drive next.
upNext.turns: Number of corners on the circuit. Keep the <n></n> tags around the number; they style it.
upNext.assistsTcOnly: TC = traction control. Usually kept as TC.
upNext.withRacingLine: {assists}: the assist level, already translated. The racing line is the drawn ideal line on the road.
title.carFixed: Shown on the car browser's main button: the car can't be changed during this online race.
title.updateLeavesRoom: Text of the 'Reload for the update?' dialog when the player is in a multiplayer room.
title.updateLeavesRace: Text of the 'Reload for the update?' dialog when the player has entered a scheduled online race.
title.editProfile: Screen-reader name of the driver-name button in the header. {name}: the player's driver name, said first.
title.inputKeyboard: Header: the input device in use now.
title.inputController: Header: the input device in use now (a gamepad).
title.inputWheel: Header: the input device in use now (a racing wheel).
title.inputTouch: Header: the input device in use now (a touch screen).
upNext.assistsPro: Driving assists level: none at all.
upNext.assistsSemiPro: Driving assists level: traction control and anti-lock brakes only. Usually kept as TC + ABS.
upNext.assistsAssisted: Driving assists level: every assist on.
panel.close: Button beside an open panel's heading: closes the panel.
supportNote.region: Screen-reader name of the note after a drive that names who made the circuit and car.
supportNote.circuit: Note after a drive. {circuit}: circuit name. {circuitMaker}: the modder's name. Names are not translated. Keep the <maker></maker> tags around the name.
supportNote.car: Note after a drive. {car}: car name. {carMaker}: who made the car's model. Keep the <maker></maker> tags.
supportNote.carRole: Note after a drive, for a car credit of another kind. {car}: car name. {role}: what the maker made, in English lower case. {carMaker}: their name. Keep the <maker></maker> tags.
supportNote.both: Note after a drive: the circuit and the car, each with its maker. Keep the <maker></maker> tags around both names.
supportNote.bothRole: As 'both', for a car credit of another kind. {role}: what the maker made, in English lower case.
supportNote.carPhysics: Note after a drive: the car's physics (driving model) are this modder's work. {car}: car name. {carMaker}: their name. Keep the <maker></maker> tags.
supportNote.bothPhysics: As 'both', when the car's maker made its physics (driving model).
supportNote.close: Screen-reader name of the note's close (X) button.
credits.moreWorks: A modder's works, shortened. {works}: the first three names, comma-separated, not translated. {count}: how many more.
credits.physicsBody: Technical summary. Keep 6-DOF, Pacejka Magic Formula, ERS and numbers as they are.
credits.graphicsBody: Technical summary. Keep WebGL2, PBR, GPU and Web Audio as they are.
credits.hudTitle: Credits heading: the third-party HUD (dashboard overlay) layouts.
credits.hudLicences: Keep THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md as it is (a file name) and the <link></link> tags around it.
credits.nissansTitle: Credits heading for two Nissan Skyline race cars.
credits.pfalzdriverTitle: Credits heading: three car names. Only 'and' is translated.
credits.sceneryTitle: Credits heading: 3D scenery placed beside the RISE Motordrome circuit (a circuit name, not translated).
credits.builtWith: Keep the product and licence names (Next.js, React, Three.js, Tailwind CSS, GNU AGPL v3.0) as they are.
browser.search: Label of the search field in the circuit and car browsers.
browser.searchPrompt: Button prompt: the key that jumps to the search field.
browser.filters: Phone button that shows the filter and sort fields.
browser.filtersActive: The Filters button when filters are set. {count}: how many. <n></n> styles the number; <sr></sr> is read by screen readers only ('2 on').
browser.count: How many items a filter choice would show. {kind}: cars or venues (circuit locations with one or more layouts).
browser.shownOf: Count under the browser, e.g. '11 of 14 venues'. {shown}: how many match; {total}: how many there are.
browser.gridLabel: Screen-reader name of the card grid. {label}: Cars or Circuits. {shownOf}: e.g. '11 of 14 venues', already translated.
browser.noMatches: Empty grid. {query}: what the player typed.
browser.noMatchesIn: Empty grid. {query}: what the player typed. {filters}: the filter choices set, comma-separated, already translated.
browser.noItemsIn: Empty grid. {filters}: the filter choices set, comma-separated, already translated.
browser.details: Screen-reader name of the side pane that shows the chosen card.
browser.detailsPrompt: Button prompt: show the highlighted card in the details pane.
browser.favourite: Tooltip of the star button when the item is already a favourite.
browser.favouritePrompt: Button prompt: star or unstar the highlighted card.
carPicker.yearCars: Screen-reader name of a group of cars from one year. {year}: e.g. 2025.
carPicker.withPhysics: {sub}: the car's short description. {physics}: the physics model's name, not translated.
carPicker.physics: Setting: which physics model the ported open-wheel cars drive on.
carBrowser.show: Filter field: which list to show (all, favourites, recently driven).
carBrowser.physicsFilter: Filter field: how a car's physics were made.
carBrowser.sortPhysics: Sort choice: by how a car's physics were made.
carBrowser.headingName: Heading over the list when it is sorted alphabetically.
carBrowser.headingRecent: Heading over the list when it is sorted by recently driven.
carBrowser.withPhysics: {facts}: the car's year and specs. {physics}: the physics model's name, not translated.
carBrowser.physicsOnly: {physics}: the physics model's name, not translated.
carBrowser.creditModel: Who made the car's 3D model. Keep the <link></link> tags around the name.
carBrowser.creditModelTyres: Who made the car's model and its tyres. Keep both tag pairs.
carBrowser.creditPhysics: Who made the car's physics (driving model). Keep the <link></link> tags.
carBrowser.creditPhysicsTyres: Who made the car's physics and its tyres. Keep both tag pairs.
carBrowser.creditOther: {label}: the credit's own English words (e.g. 'Sound by'). Keep the tags.
carBrowser.creditOtherTyres: {label}: the credit's own English words. Keep both tag pairs.
carBrowser.current: Disabled main button: this is the car being driven.
circuitBrowser.outline: Screen-reader name of the circuit's map. {circuit}: circuit name.
circuitBrowser.show: Filter field: which list to show (all, favourites, recently driven).
circuitBrowser.qualityFilter: Filter field: where the circuit's 3D model comes from.
circuitBrowser.typeFilter: Filter field: circuit or hill climb.
circuitBrowser.modderFilter: Filter field: who made the circuit (a modder is someone who makes game content).
circuitBrowser.headingName: Heading over the list when it is sorted alphabetically.
circuitBrowser.headingLength: Heading over the list when it is sorted by length.
circuitBrowser.headingRecent: Heading over the list when it is sorted by recently driven.
circuitBrowser.pbIcon: Screen-reader name of the stopwatch icon beside a personal best lap time.
circuitBrowser.oldPhysics: Tag beside a lap time set on an older version of the physics.
circuitBrowser.carOldPhysics: Tag beside a lap time: {car} is the car's short name; 'Old' means set on older physics.
circuitBrowser.layouts: Badge: how many layouts (track configurations) a circuit has.
circuitBrowser.facts: {length}: e.g. '5.34 km'. {turns}: number of corners. {direction}: clockwise or anticlockwise, already translated.
circuitBrowser.factsAltitude: As 'facts', with the circuit's altitude. 'm alt' = metres above sea level.
circuitBrowser.clockwise: Direction the circuit is driven, lower case: it goes inside a sentence.
circuitBrowser.anticlockwise: Direction the circuit is driven, lower case: it goes inside a sentence.
circuitBrowser.personalBest: Heading over the player's best lap times on this circuit.
circuitBrowser.oldPhysicsTag: Tag beside a lap time set on an older version of the physics.
circuitBrowser.layout: Setting: which layout (track configuration) of the circuit to load.
circuitBrowser.pointToPoint: A hill climb: one timed run from start to finish, driven alone.
circuitBrowser.circuitBy: {author}: who made the circuit, not translated. Keep the <name></name> tags.
circuitBrowser.active: Disabled main button: this circuit is the one loaded.
circuitBrowser.loading: Main button while the circuit loads. {circuit}: circuit name.
challenge.view: Screen-reader name of the switch between this week and the Hall of Fame.
challenge.hallOfFame: Tab: the winners of past weekly challenges.
challenge.rules: Screen-reader name of the row of rule badges (assists, realism).
challenge.about: Flying laps = timed laps started at speed. Track limits = staying inside the white lines.
challenge.drivers: Badge: how many drivers set a time. {count}: the number, already formatted.
challenge.physicsVersion: Screen-reader name of the choice of physics version for the lap board.
challenge.behindDriver: {gap}: seconds, e.g. 0.412. {driver}: the name of the driver one place ahead.
challenge.behindPlace: {gap}: seconds, e.g. 0.412. P{place}: the position one place ahead, e.g. P3.
challenge.tableLabel: Screen-reader name of the lap time table.
challenge.tableLabelVersion: Screen-reader name of the lap time table. {version}: the physics version's name.
conditions.hostSet: Badge: in multiplayer, the room's host chooses these settings.
conditions.weatherGroup: Screen-reader name of the weather choices.
conditions.now: Card heading: the live weather readings of the session running now.
conditions.clock: Readout label: the time of day in the session.
conditions.surface: Readout label: how wet the track is.
conditions.raining: {state}: Dry, Damp, Wet or Flooded, already translated.
conditions.timeOfDayGroup: Screen-reader name of the time-of-day choices.
conditions.trackOwnTime: Under a time of day: the circuit races at this time by default (a night race). {clock}: e.g. 21:00. Keep the <time></time> tags.
conditions.timeProgression: Setting: how fast the clock runs during the session.
conditions.timeFixed: Time progression choice: the clock does not move.
conditions.trackCard: Card heading: the track surface's grip settings.
conditions.gripEvolution: Setting: how fast the track gains grip as rubber is laid down.
conditions.gripStatic: Grip evolution choice: grip never changes.
conditions.realismHint: {level}: the realism level's name. {detail}: its description. Both already translated.
garage.dialTc: Car electronics: traction control level. Keep TC1 as it is.
garage.dialTc2: Car electronics: how hard traction control cuts power. Keep TC2 as it is.
garage.dialAbs: Anti-lock brakes. Usually kept as ABS.
garage.dialBias: How the braking force is split between front and rear.
garage.dialDiffEntry: Differential setting when entering a corner (off throttle).
garage.dialDiffExit: Differential setting when leaving a corner (on throttle).
garage.assistOff: Assist level shown in the Garage: no assists.
garage.assistTcAbs: Assist level: traction control and anti-lock brakes. Usually kept as TC + ABS.
garage.tabAero: Short tab name for the aerodynamics page.
garage.tabGeometry: Short tab name for the suspension geometry page.
garage.tabMechanical: Short tab name for the mechanical grip page.
garage.hintBothWays: Under a setup slider: what moving it right and left does. {right}, {left}: the effects, from the setup sheet.
garage.resetRow: Screen-reader name of a setting's reset button. {setting}: the setting's name in lower case. {value}: its baseline value.
garage.pageReset: Message after a reset. {page}: the setup page's name.
garage.listFull: {max}: the most setups that can be saved.
garage.saved: {name}: the setup's name, chosen by the player.
garage.appliedListFull: {name}: the setup's name. {max}: the most setups that can be saved.
garage.appliedSaveBlocked: {name}: the setup's name. The browser refuses to store data.
garage.tyreCompound: Setting: which tyre type the car uses (soft, medium, hard…).
garage.specCompound: {tyre}: the only tyre this car can use. A spec compound is the one tyre a racing series allows.
garage.aeroPackage: Setting: the car's wing and downforce package.
garage.balanced: Aero package between low and high downforce.
garage.assists: Setting row: traction control and anti-lock brakes (set in Settings).
garage.tcOnly: Assist level: traction control only, no ABS.
garage.noFactoryAbs: {assists}: the assist level, already translated. The car was built without anti-lock brakes.
garage.backAria: Screen-reader name of the button that returns from the car browser.
garage.back: Button that returns from the car browser to the Garage.
garage.carFixedReason: Why the Change car button is disabled during an online race.
garage.carFixed: The Change car button during an online race.
garage.name: Label of the field for a saved setup's name.
garage.shareCode: Button: copies a text code another player can paste to load this setup.
garage.shareCodeCopied: The Share code button just after copying.
garage.shareCodeTitle: Keep LC1 as it is: the code's format.
garage.import: Button: opens the field to paste a setup code.
garage.sharedSetup: Name shown for a pasted setup that has no name.
garage.builtFor: {car}: the car the pasted setup was made for. 'Clamped' = values outside this car's range are brought inside it.
garage.factory: Tag beside a setup that comes with the car.
garage.loadFactoryAria: Screen-reader name. {name}: the factory setup's name.
garage.loadAria: Screen-reader name. {name}: the saved setup's name.
garage.copyAria: Screen-reader name. {name}: the saved setup's name.
garage.deleteAria: Screen-reader name. {name}: the saved setup's name.
garage.dismiss: Screen-reader name of the X that closes a message.
garage.pages: Screen-reader name of the tabs of setup pages.
garage.changed: Screen-reader name of the dot on a setup tab: how many settings differ from the baseline.
garage.resetPage: Button: puts this page's settings back to the baseline. {count}: how many are changed.
wizard.keyboard: First-run setup step heading: setting up the keyboard.
wizard.controller: First-run setup step heading: setting up a gamepad.
wizard.wheel: First-run setup step heading: setting up a racing wheel and pedals.
wizard.device: First-run setup step heading: choose keyboard, controller, wheel or touch.
wizard.car: First-run setup step heading: pick a car.
wizard.steps: Screen-reader name of the list of setup steps.
wizard.stepDone: Screen-reader name of the tick beside a finished step.
wizard.close: Back button on the first step when setup was opened from Settings.
wizard.promptMove: Button prompt: the stick or arrow keys move the cursor.
wizard.promptSelect: Button prompt: confirm the highlighted item.
wizard.promptStep: Button prompt: shoulder buttons go to the previous or next step.
wizard.lightsOut: Last button of the first-run setup: starts driving (as the start lights go out in a race).
wizard.done: Last button when setup was opened again from Settings.
gpuLost.lostBodyLower: Low = the lowest graphics quality setting.
gpuLost.lower: Button: set graphics quality to Low and load again.
install.button: Header button on phones and tablets: install the game as an app.
install.appleTitle: iPhone/iPad: the Safari menu item 'Add to Home Screen'. Use the name iOS shows in your language.
install.appleBody: Share and Add to Home Screen are Safari's own menu items: use the names iOS shows in your language.
install.otherBody: Install app and Add to Home Screen are browser menu items: use the names browsers show in your language.
embedded.title: Tooltip when the game runs inside another website. {site}: librecorsa.org.
embedded.play: Button when the game runs inside another website. {site}: librecorsa.org.
liveLine.online: Beside the logo: how many players have the game open now. {count}: already formatted. Keep the <n></n> tags.
liveLine.drivers: Beside the logo: how many drivers have ever played. {count}: the number, already formatted. Keep the <n></n> tags.
music.group: Screen-reader name of the music controls.
music.off: Status text: the menu music is switched off.
music.titleOn: Tooltip of the button that switches the music back on.
music.titleOff: Tooltip of the button that switches the music off.
update.ready: A newer version of the game is available.
update.reload: Button: reload the page to get the new version.
update.confirmReload: Dialog button: reload the page now.
loading.tipMenu: Loading screen tip. Esc is a key name: keep it. Corner jump = moving the car to a chosen corner.
loading.tipBraking: Driving tip. Trail off = ease off the brake while turning in; the apex is the inside point of a corner.
loading.tipFreeCamera: {freeKey}, {tvKey}: key names, e.g. F7 and F8. Trackside TV = TV-style cameras beside the track.
loading.tipLine: {key}: a key name, e.g. R. The braking line is the drawn ideal line on the road.
loading.tipBoost: Boost = the hybrid battery's extra power.
loading.tipAltitude: {altitude}: metres above sea level, already formatted.
loading.shadersQueued: Loading status: shaders (graphics programs) wait their turn.
loading.assetQueued: {asset}: what is being loaded (e.g. 'Circuit model'). Queued = waiting its turn.
loading.assetProgress: {asset}: what is being loaded. {loaded}, {total}: sizes in megabytes.
loading.circuitBy: {circuit}: circuit name. {maker}: who made it. Keep the <name></name> tags.
loading.carModelBy: {car}: car name. {maker}: who made its 3D model. Keep the <name></name> tags.
loading.carPhysicsBy: {car}: car name. {maker}: who made its physics. Keep the <name></name> tags.
loading.carRoleBy: {car}: car name. {role}: what the maker made, in English lower case. Keep the <name></name> tags.
loading.gameBy: {maker}: the game's developer. Keep the <name></name> tags.
loading.donateHint: Source is the name of a button beside each circuit and car in the menus.
loading.readyAnnouncement: Read by screen readers once loading has finished.
loading.lightsOut: Screen-reader name of the start lights (a progress indicator) when loading is done.
loading.lights: Screen-reader name of the start lights (a progress indicator). {lit}: lights on; {total}: 5.
loading.drawing: Screen-reader name of the circuit map that draws itself while loading. {circuit}: circuit name.
loading.trackLine: Under the circuit name. {place}: layout and city, may be empty. {length}: e.g. '5.34 km'. {turns}: number of corners.
raceRules.aggressionClean: Hint for the AI aggression choice 'Clean'.
raceRules.aggressionNormal: Hint for the AI aggression choice 'Normal'.
raceRules.aggressionHard: Hint for the AI aggression choice 'Hard'. Dives = late overtaking moves.
raceRules.opponents: How many AI cars race against the player.
raceRules.fieldOff: AI opponents choice: no AI cars (practice alone).
raceRules.heavyField: Hint: many AI cars can make the game run slower.
raceRules.restartRace: Hint: changing the number of AI cars restarts the race.
raceRules.restartSession: Hint: choosing AI cars restarts the practice session as a race.
raceRules.qualifyingHint: Qualifying: the player drives alone; the best lap without cutting the track sets the starting position.
raceRules.gridSlot: Setting: where the player starts on the grid.
raceRules.aiGrid: Setting: the order the AI cars start in.
raceRules.aiGridHint: AI cars start by speed, shuffled a little as in qualifying.
raceRules.startHint: The racing rules decide the start type.
raceRules.launch: Setting: how the player launches the car at the start (automatic or manual clutch).
raceRules.launchRolling: Launch applies only to standing starts.
raceRules.rules: Setting: the set of racing rules (open-wheel, endurance sprint…).
raceRules.trackLimitsOff: Hint: with track limits off, only cutting a corner is penalised.
raceRules.field: Card heading: the AI cars in the race.
raceRules.aiRace: Card heading: the race against AI cars.
raceRules.aiRaceHint: The race settings apply once AI opponents are turned on.
raceRules.race: Card heading: laps, qualifying and start.
raceRules.raceApplies: Changes take effect at the next race start.
raceRules.rulesCard: Card heading: racing rules, track limits and damage.
raceRules.rulesApplies: Changes take effect at the next race start.
raceSetup.change: Button beside a race setting: change it.
raceSetup.event: Card heading: the circuit, conditions and car of the race.
raceSetup.changeCircuit: Screen-reader name of the Change button. {value}: the circuit.
raceSetup.changeConditions: Screen-reader name of the Change button. {value}: the weather and time of day.
raceSetup.conditionsAsSet: The conditions as they are set now.
raceSetup.changeCar: Screen-reader name of the Change button. {value}: the car line, already translated.
raceSetup.carForField: {car}: car name. Every car in the race is this car.
raceSetup.gridByQualifying: The grid comes from qualifying. {count}: cars in the race.
raceSetup.showGrid: Expands the starting order. {count}: cars in the race.
raceSetup.slotDrawn: The player's grid position is random, picked when the race starts.
raceSetup.summary: Bar over the Start race button. {laps}: race laps. {opponents}: AI cars.
raceSetup.summaryDistance: Bar over the Start race button. {distance}: race distance, e.g. '26.7 km'.
raceSetup.aiLine: {skill}: the AI level's name, already translated. {start}: empty, or ', ' plus the start type (e.g. ', Rolling start').
raceSetup.aiLineManual: As 'aiLine'; the player launches the car with the clutch.
feedback.kinds: Screen-reader name of the choice of report type.
feedback.kindWheel: Report type: how a racing wheel works with the game.
feedback.kindCar: Report type: ask for a car to be added.
feedback.kindTrack: Report type: ask for a circuit to be added.
feedback.sendReport: Opens the report on GitHub to send it.
feedback.licenseCc0: Licence choice. Keep CC0 as it is; public domain = no copyright.
feedback.licenseUnknown: Licence choice: the player doesn't know the licence.
feedback.permissionUnknown: Permission choice: the player doesn't know.
feedback.choose: Placeholder of a drop-down before anything is picked.
feedback.alwaysSentTitle: Tooltip of a report line that can't be left out: GitHub's issue form requires it.
feedback.alwaysSent: Screen-reader name of the lock on a report line that can't be left out.
feedback.contentRules: Keep the licence names (CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC0, CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA) and the tags.
feedback.included: Card heading: the game details added to a bug report.
feedback.rowInput: Report line: the input device (keyboard, controller, wheel).
feedback.rowDevices: Report line: the connected controllers and wheels.
feedback.rowWhere: Report line: where on the circuit the car was.
feedback.rowDrawn: Report line: the graphics settings the game draws with.
feedback.rowApp: Report line: browser, installed app or desktop app.
feedback.rowBoard: Report line: the state of the online lap boards.
feedback.rowDriver: Report line: the player's driver name.
feedback.gameLog: Report line: the game's recent error messages.
feedback.gameLogValue: {count}: lines in the log. {latest}: the newest line, in English.
feedback.trimmedDetails: After sending: some lines were too long for the GitHub link. {count}: how many.
feedback.trimmedLog: After sending: the older error messages were too long for the GitHub link. Starts in lower case in English; start it as your language needs.
feedback.trimmedBoth: After sending: {count} lines and the older errors were too long for the GitHub link.
feedback.bugWhatCount: Hint as the text gets long. {count}: characters typed, already formatted. 1,500 is the limit.
feedback.bugSteps: Field label: how to reproduce the bug. The * marks a required field.
feedback.wheelModel: Field label: the wheel base (motor unit) and rim (the wheel itself). The * marks a required field.
feedback.ideaArea: Field label: which part of the game the idea is about.
feedback.modelLink: Field label: a web link to the 3D model. The * marks a required field.
feedback.rippedTags: {tags}: the model's tags, quoted, not translated. Ripped = copied out of another game without permission.
feedback.modderSaidYesTrack: A checkbox statement. The * marks it as required. A modder is someone who makes game content.
feedback.modderSaidYesCar: A checkbox statement. The * marks it as required.
feedback.askedModdersTrack: A checkbox statement. The * marks it as required.
feedback.askedModdersCar: A checkbox statement. The * marks it as required.
feedback.screenshotAlt: Description of the screenshot taken when the report opened.
livery.group: Screen-reader name of the livery (paint scheme) choices.
livery.skinGroup: Screen-reader name of the livery (paint scheme) choices of a car with its own liveries.
livery.custom: Screen-reader name of the custom paint swatch, which opens colour pickers.
livery.slot: Name of one of a custom livery's three colours.
livery.slotInput: Screen-reader name of the colour picker for one of the three colours.
livery.slotPresets: Screen-reader name of a row of preset colours.
livery.slotPreset: Screen-reader name of a preset colour. {colour}: the colour's name.
shell.newTab: Screen-reader name of the icon on a menu link that opens in a new browser tab.
shell.resetRow: Button prompt: puts the setting under the cursor back to its default.
pad.unbound: A controller action with no button assigned.
credits.tyresTitle: Credits heading: who made the tyre models and textures.
credits.circuitsTitle: Credits heading: who made the circuit models.
browser.sort: Field label in the circuit and car browsers: how the cards are ordered.
browser.noItems: Empty grid with no search and no filters. {kind}: cars or venues (circuit locations).
carPicker.classes: Screen-reader name of the car class choice in the first-run setup.
carBrowser.label: Screen-reader name of the car browser.
carBrowser.showFavourites: Filter choice: only the cars the player starred.
carBrowser.showRecent: Filter choice: only the cars the player drove lately.
carBrowser.sortRecent: Sort choice: most recently driven first.
carBrowser.choose: Main button of the car browser: switch to this car.
circuitBrowser.label: Screen-reader name of the circuit browser.
circuitBrowser.showFavourites: Filter choice: only the circuits the player starred.
circuitBrowser.showRecent: Filter choice: only the circuits the player drove lately.
circuitBrowser.anyType: Filter choice: circuits and hill climbs.
circuitBrowser.anyModder: Filter choice: no filter by who made the circuit.
circuitBrowser.sortRegion: Sort choice: grouped by part of the world.
circuitBrowser.sortQuality: Sort choice: grouped by where the circuit's 3D model comes from.
circuitBrowser.sortRecent: Sort choice: most recently driven first.
circuitBrowser.hillClimb: Badge: a point-to-point uphill course instead of a loop.
circuitBrowser.load: Main button of the circuit browser: load this circuit.
challenge.drive: Button: drive this week's challenge (its circuit, car and rules are set up).
conditions.grip: Setting: how much grip the track surface has.
conditions.realism: Setting: how realistic the simulation is (set in Settings > Driving).
garage.lowDownforce: Aero package: less wing, faster on straights.
garage.highDownforce: Aero package: more wing, faster in corners.
garage.settings: Button: opens Settings at the driving assists.
garage.livery: Row label: the car's paint scheme.
garage.savedSetups: Card heading: car setups the player saved under a name.
garage.resetAll: Button: every setup setting back to the car's baseline.
garage.namePlaceholder: Placeholder of the field for a saved setup's name.
garage.save: Button: save the current setup under the name typed.
garage.loadFile: Button: pick a setup file (.json) to import. Keep .json as it is.
garage.apply: Button: load the pasted setup onto the car.
garage.undo: Button in a message: undo the last change.
wizard.assists: First-run setup step heading: choose driving assists.
wizard.hud: First-run setup step heading: choose the HUD (on-screen dashboard) layout.
wizard.mainMenu: Back button on the first step of the first-run setup: go to the main menu.
wizard.skip: Button: skip the rest of the setup with default choices.
gpuLost.retry: Button: load the circuit again with the same settings.
install.otherTitle: Dialog heading: how to install the game as an app.
install.gotIt: Button that closes the install instructions.
music.next: Button: skip to the next music track.
loading.compilingShaders: Loading status: preparing the graphics programs (shaders).
raceRules.qualifying: Setting: a timed session before the race that sets the starting order.
raceRules.trackLimits: Setting: penalties for driving outside the white lines.
raceRules.damage: Setting: how much collisions damage the cars.
raceRules.aiOpponents: Setting: how many computer-controlled cars race.
raceRules.aiLevel: Setting: how fast the computer-controlled cars are.
raceRules.aiAggression: Setting: how hard the computer-controlled cars race the player.
raceSetup.conditions: Row label: the race's weather and time of day.
raceSetup.car: Row label: the car everyone races.
feedback.heading: Panel heading: send a bug report, a request or an idea.
feedback.sendIdea: Button: opens the idea on GitHub to send it.
feedback.sendRequest: Button: opens the car or circuit request on GitHub to send it.
feedback.rowGraphics: Report line: graphics quality and resolution.
feedback.rowBrowser: Report line: the web browser and operating system.
feedback.rowScreen: Report line: screen and window size.
feedback.rowGpu: Report line: the graphics card. Usually kept as GPU.
feedback.rowDevice: Report line: the phone, tablet or computer.
feedback.copyPicture: Button: copy the screenshot to the clipboard.
feedback.savePicture: Button: save the screenshot as a file.
feedback.writeAnother: Button after sending: start a new report.
feedback.notes: Field label: anything else the player wants to add.
feedback.screenshot: Card heading: a picture of the game taken when the report opened.
circuitBrowser.sortPopular: Sort option: circuits driven most by all players first. Short.
circuitBrowser.headingPopular: Heading over the list sorted by Most driven. {days}: how many days are counted (30).
circuitBrowser.boardRank: The player's place on the online lap board, e.g. 'P12 of 340'. P = position; {pos} and {total} are already formatted. Keep the tags.
carBrowser.sortPopular: Sort option: cars driven most by all players first. Short.
carBrowser.headingPopular: Heading over the list sorted by Most driven. {days}: how many days are counted (30).
upNext.personalBest: Row on the title screen's Up next sheet: the player's best lap for this circuit and car.
upNext.oldPhysics: Tag beside a best lap set before the current physics. Short.
upNext.noTimeYet: Shown when the player has no lap for this circuit and car.
